The Trump administration called the tariffs "reciprocal", asserting they mirrored and counteracted trade barriers faced by U.S. exports. The items most affected by the tariffs are metals, items mostly made of metal, and vehicles. After World War II, relations evolved from the Second Cairo Conference in December 1943 and Turkey's entry into World War II on the side of the Allies in February 1945. Later that year, Turkey became a charter member of the United Nations. Since 1945, both countries have strengthened ties under the liberal international order advanced by the U.S., a set of global, rule-based, structured relationships grounded in political and economic liberalism. During the interwar period (1918–1939), Turkey and the United States laid the groundwork for cooperation without a defined strategic interest.
